FOCUSED_SUPPORT_SELECTOR_ATTEMPT.txt

The attempted operation

For an arbitrary rational matrix $M$, find

$$Mw=0,\quad w\ge0,\qquad z=-M^\top y\ge0,$$

with

$$w_i z_i=0,\qquad w_i+z_i>0\quad\text{for every }i.$$

This would select the complementary supports of the nonnegative kernel and its dual cone. A strongly polynomial implementation of this operation would solve the entire requested LP problem.

Complete reduction to the requested output types

For primal feasibility, apply the operation to $M=[A,-b]$, with last coordinate $\tau$.

- If $w_\tau>0$, then $x=w_{[n]}/w_\tau$ is feasible.

- If $w_\tau=0$, strict support coverage gives $z_\tau=b^\top y>0$. Then $f=-y$ satisfies
$$A^\top f\ge0,\qquad b^\top f<0,$$
providing the exact Farkas certificate.

Once primal feasibility is acquired, test dual feasibility in standard form:

$$[A^\top,-A^\top,I](y^+,y^-,s)=c,\qquad y^+,y^-,s\ge0.$$

An infeasibility certificate for this system is precisely a vector

$$d\ge0,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad c^\top d<0.$$

Together with the already obtained feasible point, it gives the required unboundedness output.

If both sides are feasible, a third feasibility call solves the linear zero-gap system

$$Ax=b,\quad A^\top(y^+-y^-)+s=c,\quad
c^\top x-b^\top(y^+-y^-)=0,$$

with nonnegative standard-form variables, returning exact optimal solutions.

These are a constant number of calls with polynomial dimension and encoding growth, with no coefficient-dependent search loop.
